hints.en: For each case combine two conditions with `&`: `((pred == 1) & (y == 1)).sum()`.

hints.en:
The full solution:

```python
import numpy as np


def confusion_counts(y, pred):
    y, pred = np.array(y), np.array(pred)
    tp = int(((pred == 1) & (y == 1)).sum())
    fp = int(((pred == 1) & (y == 0)).sum())
    fn = int(((pred == 0) & (y == 1)).sum())
    tn = int(((pred == 0) & (y == 0)).sum())
    return tp, fp, fn, tn

y = [1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0]
pred = [1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0]
print(confusion_counts(y, pred))
```

hint.en: Do not use `confusion_matrix`; count the four cases.
